title: Inguinal canal & hernia anatomy
claims: The inguinal canal runs from the deep ring (in transversalis fascia) to the superficial ring (in the external oblique aponeurosis), carrying the spermatic cord / round ligament.
Hesselbach triangle is bounded by the inferior epigastric vessels (lateral), the lateral border of rectus (medial) and the inguinal ligament (inferior).
Femoral triangle, lateral to medial: Nerve, Artery, Vein, (empty space) Lymphatics. The femoral sheath holds the artery, vein and femoral canal; the femoral nerve lies outside the sheath.
An indirect hernia passes through the deep ring, lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels, and follows the spermatic cord in the canal; it can reach the scrotum.
Indirect hernia is caused by a patent processus vaginalis (congenital) and is the most common hernia in both sexes.
An indirect hernia is covered by all layers of the spermatic cord fascia. Mnemonic: "MD's don't lie": Medial = Direct, Lateral = indirect.
A direct hernia bulges through Hesselbach triangle, medial to the inferior epigastric vessels; it is an acquired weakness of the transversalis fascia.
Direct hernia is seen in older men, heavy lifting, chronic cough/straining; it does not follow the cord through the deep ring and rarely reaches the scrotum.
A femoral hernia goes through the femoral canal, below the inguinal ligament and medial to the femoral vein.
Femoral hernia is more common in women; its narrow neck gives the highest risk of strangulation and it needs urgent repair.
